_note: Every coefficient below is copied verbatim (as a decimal string) from the source named in its block. Nothing is guessed. Strings are converted to Arb balls containing the exact decimal.

bosch_hale_DT_reactivity.source: Wurzel-Hsu public code github.com/swurzel/lawson-criterion-paper commit 4ae563bfc409db5fb4afb2f9930a3a4fafba4f0d, lib/reactions.ini section [T(d,n)4He] (sha256 be8bf1b8...e88d), formula lib/reactivity.py _reactivity_bosch_hale (Bosch-Hale 1992 eqs 12-14 per the code comment). Primary paper Bosch & Hale, Nucl. Fusion 32, 611 (1992) NOT obtained (closed access).
bosch_hale_DT_reactivity.units: C1 in cm^3/s, T in keV, BG in keV^1/2, mcsquared in keV

bosch_hale_DT_cross_section.source: same code file, CM cross-section coefficients of section [T(d,n)4He] and [T(d,n)4He_HIGH_ENERGY]; used ONLY in the Tier X float cross-check of the 'integrated' code path

nevins_swain_pB11_reactivity_highT.source: Wurzel-Hsu public code (same commit), lib/reactions.ini section [11B(p,4He)4He4He] P1..P7, EG, Mrc2 and lib/reactivity.py _reactivity_nevins_swain_pb11 (high-T branch + resonant term 5.41e-21 T^-3/2 exp(-148/T) m^3/s). Primary paper Nevins & Swain, Nucl. Fusion 40, 865 (2000) NOT obtained (IOP bot challenge / paywall); abstract (via WebFetch of the IOP landing page) states validity 50 keV <= T <= 500 keV for the high-temperature form.
nevins_swain_pB11_reactivity_highT.output_units: m^3/s as implemented in the code (code adds the m^3/s resonant term without conversion; values ~3.4e-22 m^3/s at 300 keV)

nevins_swain_pB11_S_factor_lowE.source: Wurzel-Hsu code [11B(p,4He)4He4He] C0,C1,C2,AL,EL,delEL; independently reprinted (identical values) in Wang, Li, Wu, Cui, arXiv 2601.00241 Table I (E <= 0.4 MeV), which states it follows Nevins-Swain. Used only for the Tier X NS fit-vs-integral consistency check.
nevins_swain_pB11_S_factor_lowE.units: S in MeV b, energies in keV, A_k in MeV b keV^2 (as used in lib/cross_section.py)

wang2026_pB11_S_factor.source: Wang, Li, Wu, Cui, 'Revisiting p-11B Fusion: Updated Cross-sections, Reactivity, and Energy Balance', arXiv 2601.00241v1 (1 Jan 2026), eqs (1)-(6) and Table I, read in full via alphaXiv on 2026-10-27. Licence of the arXiv preprint not stated in the text read; coefficients are cited, not redistributed as a dataset.

seg3.units: B, A_k in MeV b; Breit-Wigner A_k/(((E-E_k)/1keV)^2+(dE_k/1keV)^2)

wang2026_pB11_S_factor.reactivity_definition: eq (6): <sigma v> = (8/pi)^1/2 mu^-1/2 (kT)^-3/2 int_0^inf sigma E exp(-E/kT) dE; model support 0-10 MeV (sigma := 0 above 10 MeV, our reading of the stated fit range)

bremsstrahlung.wurzel_hsu_code_CB: 1.69e-32 cm^3 J eV^-1/2 s^-1 (NRL formulary) => 1.69e-38*sqrt(1000) W m^3 keV^-1/2; keV conversion uses 6.24e18 eV/J
bremsstrahlung.ochs_fisch_eq14_prefactor: 7.56e-11 eV cm^3/s times x^1/2, x=Te/E_rest, E_rest=5.11e5 eV
bremsstrahlung.relativistic_form: gamma = Zeff(1+1.78 t^1.34) + 2.12 t (1 + 1.1 t + t^2 - 1.25 t^2.5), t = Te/m_e c^2 (Wurzel-Hsu eq D2; Ochs-Fisch eq 14; Putvinski eq 7 as seen in WebFetch OCR)
bremsstrahlung.Zeff_definition: sum n_i Z_i^2 / n_e (W-H eq 41 / D3) = sum n_i Z_i^2 / sum n_i Z_i (Ochs-Fisch) under quasineutrality

pB11_energy.note: 8.7 MeV: W-H eq (5), W-H code, Wang 2026; 8.68 MeV: Putvinski (WebFetch OCR of TAE flipbook page 2, not a primary read)
